pairs.subject: feed
pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/view.ts:103 Runs draws every job as a bar placed by its start and end on a horizontal time axis, grouped by resource lane (a Gantt-style day-line), and the inspector groups jobs by state (failed / at the weir / running). There is no newest-first list of occurrences read top-down to catch up, so the feed subject's precondition does not hold. A case-insensitive search of app/(studio)/projects/runs for unseen, unread, prepend, lastSeen, markRead and role="log" found nothing.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/view.ts:126 The only ordered sequence is the J/K walk, ascending by start with a key tiebreak (a total order). It is keyboard navigation over a timeline, not a newest-first feed.

app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/liveFeed.ts:4 The 'live feed' is SSE advice that triggers a coalesced router.refresh() of the server render. No rows are prepended above a reading position, so there is no viewport to hold still. The realtime-events subject governs this, not feed.

app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/Runs.tsx:367 Occurrences render as lane bars on a time axis, so a busy producer takes up lane space instead of feed rows. There is no consecutive-row stream to cluster.

app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/model.ts:38 The visible past is a fixed time window around NOW over the ledger, which is the durable record. The screen stores no feed rows of its own, so it has nothing to reap. The caps (LEDGER_CAP, KERNEL_CAP) are reported as ErrorLine problems in load.ts.

app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/Runs.tsx:333 The only badge on the screen shows how fresh the render is (stale or current). No read anchor or unseen count exists, and the search found no unseen/unread/lastSeen.

pairs.registryProposal: The feed golden path could add a boundary against time-axis timelines and Gantt day-lines. These surfaces lay occurrences out by time on a horizontal axis, with lanes, and do not stack them newest-first. Teams also call them 'live feeds' because they refresh from an event stream. The tell is that position encodes duration and resource, not reading order, so data-viz/canvas-graph governs them rather than feed.
